No gate checks the evidence arrays of this file -- the trail gates read record files, and `record-reproducibility.mjs` proves declared paths for records only -- which is why this went unreported.
  * Resolving, and recorded so they are not mistaken for defects: the one 40-hex token that is not a commit in this repository is `591264f9bd4f…`, declared under `cross_repo_integration.main`, repo `berlinguyinca/herdr-engineering` -- the tip of that repository, a different checkout by design; the 23 64-hex tokens are `sha256:` content hashes, never git objects. `.github/workflows/ci.yml` is named as the file `85b1b064` removed, which is what the text says.

The suite is green on the runtime CI pins and red on a newer one, and nothing in the repository says so. Measured at e008b3dc on one laptop: `npm run test:integration` on the machine's default Node v26.3.0 answers 1185 tests / 1182 pass / 3 fail, exit 1; the same two files on v22.22.3 (CI pins NODE_VER=22.23.4, .woodpecker/ci.yaml:61) answer 16 tests / 0 fail, exit 0. The failures are `test/integration/planner-worker-gateway-timeouts.test.ts:35` (both tests die in undici's `new Dispatcher1Wrapper` with `InvalidArgumentError: Argument dispatcher must implement dispatch`) and `test/integration/planner-worker-executor.test.ts:110` (`independent contracts must run concurrently (max in flight 1)`). `package.json` declares no `engines` field, so a contributor on a newer Node gets three red tests and no statement of which runtime is the contract. Also recorded because the measurement was nearly wrong: capturing `exit=$?` after a `$(basename ...)` substitution in the same word reports basename's status, not the test runner's -- the first pass of this experiment printed rc=0 next to two failing tests.

The P5 hash re-derivation that X16/logs/10 records as self-verification did not run: the log's P5 section is a crash trace (npx tsx -e, Node v26.3.0), and the substitute check below it compared 46a7109b against itself while labelling it 'X15/out-chain's declared base' -- which is 2eee4d1a. The independent review of 2026-11-10 (X16/logs/16, finding F1) supplies the derivation the log claimed to contain: X14/out-chain, X15/out, X15/out-chain and X16/out all recompute their declared handoffHash exactly from their bytes (X16/logs/16, P5 table). Log 10 is a historical record and is not rewritten; this caveat is where the correction stands.

X15/out-chain's taskAuthorityHash (sha256:9766e2fb5a7ad9cc8..., carried by X16) breaks the FIX-4A rule it is supposed to serve: the protocol (src/bootstrap/resultGate.ts:47-54) defines authority as the canonical hash of the PARSED manifest (defaults applied, unknown keys dropped), but X15's value is the canonical hash of the RAW X15/fixtures/manifest.json bytes -- reproducible from a stored object, under the wrong canonicalization (the parsed manifest hashes to sha256:1352fe82feab5b56...). X14's record follows the protocol (its value equals its parsed-manifest hash). The comment in X16/fixtures/emit-records.mts that explained the field used to claim no stored object reproduces the value and that X14/X15 have no manifests; both halves were false and are corrected in the same PR that records this caveat (independent review finding F4, X16/logs/16). No gate reads taskAuthorityHash, and the record is hash-bound, so the deviation is declared here rather than corrected in the bytes.

E01's predecessor hash cannot be verified from the current tree: E01/out/E01.handoff.json's notes claim 'B05 handoff sha256:21bae9f5a1c1... verified by the CLI before this handoff was emitted', and E01/fixtures/manifest-e01.json declares the same value as parentHandoffHash, but the only tracked B05 record (B05/out-backfill/B05.handoff.json) hashes to sha256:064b4e712f84... -- the pre-backfill B05 record that carried 21bae9f5... is not in the tree. A mechanical sweep found this is the only unresolvable declaration: 70 of the 71 parentHandoffHash values across the trail's manifests resolve to a tracked record hash. The B05->E01 seam is still connected structurally (B05.nextBaseSha == E01.baseSha), and the protocol (02-HANDOFF-PROTOCOL.md:9) does require the predecessor hash to be verified -- which this one cannot be. Declared by the independent review of 2026-11-10 (finding F5, X16/logs/16); no gate checks parentHandoffHash, which is the gap that let it stand.

x16-controls.sh's exit status was not evidence: the script used set -u without -e, compared no case result against an expectation, and ended in echoes, so it exited 0 whether or not the scanner detected anything -- while X16/out/X16.handoff.json records its exitCode 0 as a proof. The independent review of 2026-11-10 (finding F7, X16/logs/16) found that, and the script now declares an expectation per case (exit class plus output marker) and exits 1 on any mismatch; a clean run prints 'RESULT ok: every case behaved as declared' and a deliberate expectation break exits 1 with EXPECTATION-FAILED (both measured, X16/logs/16). The recorded exitCode 0 in the X16 record therefore stands as a fact about that run only; the detections it vouches for are re-established by the asserting version.

The gates count generation records differently by construction, and a reader can misread it: integrity-scan reports in generations=121 (every file in a generation directory, including the two *.SUPERSEDED-*.json copies in FIX-4A/out and FIX-4B/out), while lineage-scan and record-reproducibility report generation=119 (only *.handoff.json). The two SUPERSEDED files are hash-checked by integrity-scan and by nothing else -- no gate walks commit pointers inside a file that is not a record. Reconciled and declared by the independent review of 2026-11-10 (finding F9, X16/logs/16).
